referents.why: 'It burst forth' in the infinitive: the sea, the masculine singular noun that bursts out of the womb. The womb is not the one bursting.
Implied third masculine singular subject of the wayyiqtol 'he shut off', in a rhetorical question about who enclosed the sea: the LORD. Not in this verse's candidate list (see cant_tell).
Implied third masculine singular subject of 'came forth' in the when-clause: the sea that bursts forth.
referents.category: implied subject in a temporal clause

links.why: The infinitive 'burst forth' is nested in the when-clause.
A clause cannot follow itself. This is a parser self-loop with no support in the form.
The when-clause 'when it burst forth from the womb' sets the time of the act in cl0 ('shut off ... the sea'): a temporal role nested in the act.
links.category: temporal clause nested in an act

cant_tell.what: The candidate list for 38:8 omits the LORD (Job.38.1#w2) and Job (Job.38.1#w4), which 38:2 to 38:7 offer. The choice for cl0s is made from the speech, not from the list.
cant_tell.why: The list is shorter than in earlier verses, so the choice is flagged for review.
